title: A Look at How Many Cancers Are Caused by Infections Worldwide - Nautilus
gist: A new Lancet Oncology study estimates worldwide rates of cancers caused by pathogens, finding nearly one in eight cancers are caused by infections — a field shaped by Barry Marshall's self-experiment proving H. pylori causes ulcers and stomach cancer.

insights.claim: Nearly one in eight cancers worldwide are caused by a pathogen, according to coverage of a new Lancet Oncology study on global rates of infection-caused cancers.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Infection-driven cancers are largely preventable via vaccines, antibiotics and screening — a sizable addressable market for prevention.
insights.quote: Nearly one in eight cancers are caused by a pathogen
insights.locator: A Look at How Many Cancers

insights.claim: Microbiologist Barry Marshall proved stomach ulcers are primarily caused by Helicobacter pylori by drinking a beaker of the bacteria and developing peptic ulcer symptoms within days.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Classic example of contrarian science overturning consensus treatment paradigms.
insights.quote: he drank a beaker full of the bugs

insights.claim: Further research showed Helicobacter pylori can also cause stomach cancer, and Barry Marshall and Robin Warren won a Nobel Prize for their work.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Eradicating H. pylori is a cancer-prevention lever.

insights.claim: Beyond bacteria, viruses and even parasites can cause cancer; the genetic underpinnings of cancer research began with a chicken virus over a century ago.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Broad pathogen-cancer link supports oncology vaccine and anti-infective research.
